newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to halve approval time on foreign funds.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to halve approval time on foreign funds.

text.p: Taiwan's top economic policy-making body said on Thursday the central bank and the Securities and Exchange Commission have agreed to speed up screening and approval procedures on foreign equity funds.

"The central bank and the SEC have agreed to cut by half the screening procedures on inflows of foreign equity funds, a step forward in our financial liberalisation," said an official at the cabinet's Council for Economic Planning and Development.
The central bank and the SEC will jointly screen applications by foreign funds, aiming to halve the present approval time of three weeks, he said.
Analysts said the move would help attract more foreign fund inflows.

"Such liberalisation will surely help attract more foreign fund entries as it will help foreign funds catch the investment timing in such a volatile local stock market," said Michael Hung, an independent analyst.
"It's a pretty positive move for the local stock market," Hung said.
Currently, foreign investors are allowed to invest in Taiwan stocks up to 25 percent of the bourse's market value.
